items.title: Nvidia extends its $2.7 trillion rout as the SEC is reported to be probing its accounting
items.take: Nvidia fell 14% Friday, its worst day since the DeepSeek rout in January 2025 and its seventh straight loss, after Reuters reported the SEC's probe is examining the chipmaker's accounting. Shares bounced about 4% after hours, and the rout lands amid leadership upheaval following Jensen Huang's exit.

items.title: S&P 500 correction: Five forces behind the market sell-off
items.take: The S&P 500 and Dow closed in correction territory Friday, more than 10% below their records, and the Nasdaq is now in the red for 2026. CNBC lays out the five forces behind the sell-off and notes Anthropic closed the week at $88.91 after the Nasdaq's worst week since March 2020.

items.title: Chips suffer their worst week since 2001 as the Nasdaq nears a bear market
items.take: Chip stocks are falling almost as fast as they did in late 2008, a pace topped only by the dot-com bust and the financial crisis. The Nasdaq 100 finished just shy of a bear market, and the S&P 500 is headed for its worst November since 1973.

items.title: Anthropic came within 5 cents of its $83 IPO price on day two, then bounced
items.take: Anthropic nearly gave back its entire debut on its second day, trading within five cents of the $83 IPO price before a late-day bounce. The piece's yardstick: Facebook fell 11% on its own day two in 2012 and closed below its IPO price.

items.title: A 10% drop for the stock market is unnerving, but it's not that unusual
items.take: The market's 10% slide from last month's high is driven by worries about the hurdles facing the AI industry. AP's read: unnerving but historically normal, with analysts likening it to the corrections of March 2020 and April 2025.
